question: What did Spinoza say a stone in flight would believe, if it could think?
answer: That it moves freely, of its own will. In a 1674 letter Spinoza argued that a thrown stone, aware of its effort to keep moving but not of the hand behind it, would call itself free. People are alike: conscious of desires, blind to their causes. A drunkard, he adds, thinks he talks freely.
move: Feeling that nothing pushed you is not evidence that nothing did.
ask: What do I call my free choice only because I cannot see what pushed me?
reference: Spinoza, The Letters, trans. Shirley, Hackett, 1995
